literal: As for all rewards and bestowals, there were no longer any limits; the accumulations of the treasury were eventually emptied.
idiomatic: Rewards and bestowals knew no limit, and the treasury's stores were drained empty.

literal: From the Empress Dowager and the princes to meritorious elders within and without the court, all were anxious, fearful, and peril-stricken, with no plan to escape.
idiomatic: From the Empress Dowager and the princes to meritorious elders within and without the court, all lived in dread and peril, with nowhere to turn.

literal: By his final years he could no longer take food and drank wine only; fermented malt became a calamity, and so he died.
idiomatic: In his final years he could no longer eat and drank only wine; fermented malt became his ruin, and he died of it.

literal: Commentary: The Grand Ancestor pacified the four barbarian peoples, and his authority endured for generations.
idiomatic: Commentary: The Grand Ancestor pacified the four barbarian peoples, and his authority endured for generations.

literal: After the move to Ye, though the heir's vessel was held by another, every command issued and every policy came from himself.
idiomatic: After the move to Ye, though an heir held the vessel of state, every command and every policy still issued from the regent alone.

literal: The Founding Ancestor inherited the great enterprise; inner and outer aligned in obedience, from court to countryside all hearts looked to him.
idiomatic: The Founding Ancestor inherited the great enterprise; court and countryside alike fell into step, and every heart turned toward him.

literal: Throughout the lands of Eastern Wei all gladly urged him forward; not even a full month had passed before the dark mandate gathered upon him.
idiomatic: Throughout Eastern Wei all gladly urged him forward; before a month had passed the dark mandate had gathered upon him.

literal: At first he applied his mind to government; customs grew solemn and upright, and within a few years he brought order together.
idiomatic: At first he gave his mind to government; customs grew solemn and upright, and within a few years he had brought the realm to order.

literal: Afterward he gave free rein to wine and desire, indulging to the utmost in madness; his delusion, wickedness, cruelty, and ferocity were unmatched in recent ages.
idiomatic: Afterward he gave free rein to wine and desire, indulging madness to the limit; his delusion, wickedness, cruelty, and ferocity were unmatched in recent memory.

literal: That he did not long enjoy the realm was truly due to this malady; the extinction of his heirs was likewise the lingering curse of it.
idiomatic: That he did not long enjoy the realm was truly due to this sickness; the extinction of his line was likewise the lingering curse of it.

literal: Appraisal: In the Tianbao reign the throne was fixed; to receive the end of the mandate was his allotted portion.
idiomatic: Appraisal: In the Tianbao reign the throne was fixed; to receive the mandate's end was his allotted portion.

literal: He took possession of the central lands and thereupon received the imperial tally.
idiomatic: He took possession of the central lands and thereupon received the imperial tally.

literal: The momentum matched the people's song of praise; yet the sentiment later ruined the jade tally and regalia.
idiomatic: The momentum matched the people's song of praise; yet in the end his heart ruined the jade tally and regalia.

literal: At first he preserved the art of government, and men heard his virtuous words.
idiomatic: At first he preserved the art of government, and men heard his virtuous words.

literal: He did not keep to self-restraint and so gave his heart full license.
idiomatic: He did not keep to self-restraint and gave his heart full license.

literal: He pushed reason to cruelty and indulgence to the utmost in debauchery.
idiomatic: He pushed reason to cruelty and indulgence to the utmost in debauchery.

literal: The full text uses the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi, November 1972, as the base for collation.
idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju first edition of the Book of Northern Qi (November 1972).
